title: Anatomy of an Environmental Monitoring Station
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Click through the eleven components of a small weather station, name the quantity each one measures, and see which chapter covers it in depth.

educational.topic: Anatomy of an Environmental Monitoring Station
learningObjectives: Identify each major component of an environmental monitoring station.
Name the quantity each component measures.
Locate where in the book each component is covered in depth.

keyQuestions: Which components measure something, and which ones just keep the station alive?
What would the temperature reading do if the radiation shield were removed?
Why does a weather station need a GPS antenna when it never moves?
commonMisconceptions: Assuming the enclosure is just a box, rather than part of the measurement.
Thinking one sensor measures one quantity - the BME280 measures three.
Overlooking power and communications as part of the system.
assessmentOpportunities: Names all eleven components and the quantity each one measures.
Explains why the thermometer needs a radiation shield.
Identifies which components are about power and communications rather than sensing.
